subject: owl
pitch: A great horned owl perched on a gnarled branch. Mottled bark-brown and buff feathers with fine dark barring, a pale bib at the throat, tall feathered ear tufts, a round tawny facial disc rimmed in black, huge orange eyes and a hooked grey beak. Feathered legs end in strong black talons gripping the wood.
reasoning:
I'm planning the owl's proportions and the branch it perches on, working out dimensions so the branch sits flush with the ground and the owl's feet rest properly on top of it.

Now I'm sketching the skeleton: a hips root joint with a spine chain curving from tail base up through the body to the neck, using a sweep with varying radii to shape an upright egg-like torso.

For the head, I'm placing a joint above the spine's end and flattening a scaled sphere to form it, deciding to skip orientation aiming and instead just position and scale the mesh directly along world axes to keep things simple.

Now I'm defining the color palette (browns, buffs, tawny, cream, orange, grey, black) and setting up the body's paint pattern -- mottling the base coat, adding belly barring stripes, and compositing a custom paint function to shade the front of the belly differently.

I'm thinking through the throat bib (a pale cream patch near the beak) and the facial disc shape, likely using flattened spheres or short cylinders positioned on either side of the head to mimic an owl-like face.

Still positioning facial features, including a darker rim behind the tawny disc and placing the orange eye spheres with black pupils so they protrude slightly from the disc surface.

Now I'm working out the brow as an angled dark slab above the eyes, and shaping the hooked beak from an angled cone with a separate lower jaw piece for articulation.

I'm positioning the lower beak and jaw bone so the beak sits centered in the seam between the facial discs without gaps, then adding tufted ear cones tilted outward with a darker front stripe and lighter inner layer for a two-tone feather effect.

Now I'm working out the folded wing shape, planning to extrude a leaf-like outline running from shoulder to tail along the body's side profile with a beveled thickness for a natural curved look.

Adding wing joints with a "wing" role parented to the spine, then starting the tail chain hanging down and back for a perched posture.

I'm striping the tail coloring by z-axis rings, then working out the branch geometry — keeping it along x at z=0, gnarled but with its centerline and radius staying just above y=0 so it doesn't dip below the ground plane.

Now I'm setting up the legs: a hip-to-ankle chain with bend direction forward at the knee, feathered thigh tapering with a barred buff color, and feet positioned near the branch with toes as three forward rods and one back.

I'm figuring out toe geometry with tan feathered rods and small curved black talon cones at the tips, having the toes wrap over the branch's top curvature using a bezier-like path from foot position down over the front of the branch.

Working out the toe placement now: three front toes fanned with slight x offsets and one back toe pointing opposite, each defined by a path that starts at the foot and curves forward and down over the branch surface.

I need to grab the foot joint from the leg chain's tip, and I'm checking that the hip-to-ankle distance is within reach of the thigh and shin bone lengths. Now I'm adding feathered geometry: a buffed sphere at the hip for thigh feathers and a swept tube around the leg for tarsus feathering.

With the body facing +X, I'm placing a cream bib ellipsoid near the throat, checking it sits just outside the body surface at that height, and deciding to skip a dark necklace ring and extra feather cards since paint already covers barring. I'm now setting up a sweep along the spine chain to build the main body coat.

Still writing bone and chain setup...

Still writing branch geometry...

Adjusting ear tuft placement, then adding a darker front stripe accent. For paint logic, I'm keeping head mottling simple since belly stripe conditions don't apply at that height, and setting up wing stripes running along the z-axis for a banded pattern.

Now I'm shaping the wing outline as an extruded polygon with jagged tip points, positioning it against the body so the thickness and radius line up without clipping, checking that the wingtip clears the tail area.
